chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The milk of the Jewess, the Christian woman, and the Magian woman is more pleasing to me than the milk of the child of fornication (Zina). And he did not see any harm in the child of fornication if the master of the slave girl who had illicit relations with the slave girl was considered permissible (in terms of lineage/ownership).

And cohabitation (or living together) with the Magian woman is disliked, and there is no harm in cohabitation with the Jewess and the Christian woman if they are prevented from drinking wine and other forbidden things.

key_terms.لَبَنُ: Milk (used in context of breastfeeding/legal kinship)

ai.seo_question: What is the juristic preference for milk from Jewish, Christian, and Magian women compared to the child of fornication, and what are the rules for cohabitation with them?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a hierarchy of legal purity in breastfeeding (radha'), preferring the milk of polytheists and People of the Book over that of a woman of fornication, thereby linking spiritual status to juridical validity. He further distinguishes between cohabitation (muzayara) with Magians, which is disliked, and with Jews and Christians, which is permissible provided they abstain from wine and other forbidden substances, reflecting the practical application of dhimmi laws in early Shia jurisprudence.
